component.name: Apache Santuario XML Security for Java
component.description: Java library (org.apache.santuario:xmlsec) implementing the W3C XML Signature and XML Encryption standards plus the JSR-105 javax.xml.crypto API. Consumed in-process by applications and frameworks (notably WS-Security stacks: WSS4J, CXF, OpenSAML/Shibboleth) to sign, verify, encrypt, and decrypt XML. It ships a mature DOM-based stack and a newer StAX (streaming) stack; the security-critical operations are verification and decryption of attacker-controlled XML. The threat model is a DRAFT under maintainer review (2026-06-10), not yet ratified.

externalReferences.comment: Source security model document; this file is a structured translation of it.

blueprints.name: In-process XML signature/encryption processing
blueprints.description: The library runs inside a trusted calling application. The defining trust split: the calling application is trusted; the XML input submitted for verification or decryption is untrusted and adversary-controlled. Everything in that document (elements, Reference URIs, Transform chains, KeyInfo, EncryptedKey, algorithm identifiers, namespace prefixes) must be treated as hostile. Verified/decrypted results are handed back to the caller, who must still check WHO signed and WHAT was signed.

assets.name: xmlsec library (DOM and StAX stacks)
assets.description: DOM XML Signature verification (XMLSignature.checkSignatureValue, SignedInfo), DOM XML Encryption decryption (XMLCipher), the StAX streaming stack (InboundXMLSec, input processors), transforms/canonicalization, key resolution (KeyResolver over attacker-supplied KeyInfo), and the JSR-105 API surface. All of these process untrusted XML; signing/encryption of the caller's own trusted data is only partially in the model.

zones.name: XML suppliers
zones.description: The party that supplies the XML being verified or decrypted: a network peer in a WS-Security/SAML exchange, or the sender of a signed document. Full control of the XML structure, transforms, KeyInfo, and algorithms; able to craft signature-wrapping, transform, key-confusion, decryption-oracle, and resource-exhaustion payloads.

zones.name: Calling application
zones.description: The trusted application or framework that invokes the library in-process and owns key trust, signature-coverage checking, and its own XML toolchain after extraction.

assumptions.description: A conformant JRE with a JAXP XML parser and a JCE provider for the crypto primitives; the library relies on the platform parser's DTD/entity controls.
Primitive correctness (RSA/AES/SHA, GCM nonce handling) is the JCE provider's responsibility; the library composes primitives.
XMLSignature/XMLCipher instances are not assumed thread-safe; per-operation instances are the expected usage.

Secure validation mode is the load-bearing configuration: a finding is in-model only if reachable from the untrusted XML during verify/decrypt with secure validation enabled. Whether secure validation is on by default depends on entry point and version (JSR-105 vs native path); this is the model's most important open question (Q6).

threats.name: XXE / external entity resolution during parse or verify
threats.description: An external entity resolved from the attacker's XML during parsing or verification, leading to SSRF or local file read. Secure validation rejects DOCTYPE and external entity resolution and disables RetrievalMethod/KeyInfo remote dereferencing. Severity: critical.

threats.name: Code execution or remote fetch via a dangerous Transform
threats.description: XSLT and other code-executing or remote-dereferencing transforms run on attacker XML during signature verification. Secure validation forbids dangerous transforms, notably XSLT. Severity: critical.

threats.name: Signature accepted under a weak algorithm or undersized key
threats.description: A signature accepted under MD5, truncated HMAC, or an undersized RSA key. Secure validation enforces minimum key sizes and rejects known-weak digest/MAC/signature algorithms, folding in the historical CVE mitigations. Severity: critical.

threats.name: Resource exhaustion via Reference/Transform expansion
threats.description: Super-linear CPU/memory blowup from many Reference or Transform elements in the attacker's XML. Secure validation caps the number of Reference/Transform elements to bound expansion (exact caps to be confirmed by maintainers, Q7).

threats.name: Signature forgery / cryptographic verification bypass
threats.description: An invalid signature verifies as true given a well-formed signature and a provided key, violating the cryptographic correctness of the verify/decrypt operation, the library's core function. Severity: critical.

threats.name: XML Signature Wrapping (XSW)
threats.description: A valid signature over SOME element is not a signature over the element the application cares about; the library verifies that referenced content has a valid digest but does not decide whether the RIGHT content was signed. XSW lives entirely in this gap and is the number one real-world Santuario-adjacent vulnerability class; checking that the signature covers the security-relevant elements is the caller's responsibility. False friend: 'the signature verified' is not 'the document is authentic and unmodified where it matters'.

threats.name: Key confusion via unvalidated KeyInfo
threats.description: The library resolves keys from the message's attacker-supplied KeyInfo as a convenience, not a trust decision. It does not decide whether the key is trusted; certificate-path validation or key allow-listing is the caller's responsibility. A report that boils down to 'I trusted a self-signed cert in KeyInfo' is out of model / by design.

threats.name: Processing untrusted XML with secure validation off
threats.description: With secure validation disabled, XXE, XSLT transforms, weak algorithms, and unbounded expansion are all reachable, by design, for backward-compatible processing of trusted XML. Findings requiring secure validation to be off do not meet the model's reachability precondition and are out of model (non-default build, pending Q6 on defaults).

threats.name: Protocol-level decryption oracles and replay
threats.description: The library performs the cryptographic decrypt; padding-oracle, replay, and decrypt-then-verify ordering defences are protocol-level (WS-Security/SAML) concerns that the caller's stack must handle. No decryption-oracle hardening is provided at the protocol layer.

threats.name: Compromised caller, JCE-provider flaws, side channels, retired components
threats.description: Out of scope: an attacker who controls the calling process or the trust/keystore configuration (they have already won); side-channel or co-tenant adversaries against the JCE provider; an attacker who can make the caller disable secure validation or skip trust checks; the retired C++ project and the two archived repos; and the application's XML toolchain after extraction of decrypted/verified content.

trustBoundaries.name: Untrusted XML input boundary
trustBoundaries.description: The boundary is the XML document submitted for verification or decryption: structure, Reference URIs, Transform chains, KeyInfo, EncryptedKey, and algorithm identifiers are all attacker-controlled. The triager's reachability test: a finding is in-model only if reachable from the untrusted XML during verify/decrypt with secure validation enabled.

controls.name: Secure validation mode
controls.description: The load-bearing configuration (XMLSignature/XMLCipher.setSecureValidation(true), the org.apache.xml.security.secureValidation property, on by default in some JSR-105 paths). With secure validation on, the library rejects DTDs and external entity / RetrievalMethod / remote KeyInfo dereferencing, forbids dangerous transforms (notably XSLT), enforces minimum key sizes and rejects known-weak digest/MAC/signature algorithms (MD5, SHA-1 in signatures, short RSA, HMAC truncation), and caps the number of Reference/Transform elements. Callers must enable it for any XML from outside their trust boundary; whether it is on by default per entry point/version is the model's key open question.

controls.name: Check what was signed (XSW defence)
controls.description: The caller must verify that the signature's References resolve to the exact content about to be trusted, preferring ID-based references the caller controls and re-checking post-verify, to defeat XML Signature Wrapping. Never use verification as authorization without binding the signer identity to an authorization decision.

controls.name: Establish key trust independently
controls.description: The caller must validate the certificate chain or match the resolved key against an allow-list; never trust KeyInfo-embedded keys or certificates implicitly.

controls.name: Treat decrypted/verified output as untrusted
controls.description: Treat decrypted or verified bytes as untrusted until the caller's own validation passes, and apply resource limits at the boundary.

controls.name: Protect signing and decryption private keys
controls.description: Caller-side key management: protect the private keys used for signing and decryption.
